simple.note: ALWAYS cheaper than the baseline, every model in the pool, not just the head; ceiling 0.5x, asserted for every simple pool by tests/test_router_pools.py

medium.note: leads BELOW the baseline (operator directive 2026-10-28, cycle 13902: always cheaper, except very complex work); the baseline stays in-pool as the fallback

hard.note: the exception for very complex work, but BUDGET-CAPPED at an absolute $3.00/M: only models on hard_whitelist may be routed, and nothing dearer than the cap is present in this file (the closed frontier seats - gemini-4-argon $12/M, gpt-5.3-codex $15.75/M, muse-wonder $24/M - were removed on Luke's directive 2026-10-28). Expressed absolutely, not as a multiple of the baseline, so a cheaper baseline cannot evict a good model.

policy.rejected_reason: 5.47x the baseline ($4.100/M vs the list's own $0.750/M baseline at baseline_price_usd_per_m) for a medium coding turn; the suggested pool order put it first. The ratio is checkable inside THIS FILE: this file's own rejected entry for kimi-k2.7-code records in_usd_per_m 0.60 and out_usd_per_m 3.50, so the blended $4.100/M is that entry's own 0.60 + 3.50, and 4.1 / baseline_price_usd_per_m 0.750 = 5.47, which equals the ratio_of_baseline 5.47 stored in the same entry. The component values were taken from the live catalog scan this cycle applied; kimi is deliberately absent from this file's prices block because it is rejected by policy, not routed.
policy.rule: Every pool must LEAD with a model cheaper than the baseline. Every model in a SIMPLE pool is cheaper than the baseline. A medium pool may carry the baseline as the in-pool fallback. `hard` may lead dearer - that is the exception for very complex work - but only from the hard whitelist and never above $3.00/M.

effort.note: trivial->low, routine->low, substantial->medium, expert->high. Chosen over [none,low,medium,high] because none on a confident-trivial tool-needing turn is the recorded regression (upstream jevkit/effort.py: a live fleet turn answered without calling a single tool when thinking was off); low on trivial buys most of the saving without that failure. One config value flips back if the operator wants none.
